interactions.summary: Jiang answers the question about ordinary vows by saying fully human life requires a daily habit of making vows to oneself, because vows train hope, love, faith, and movement toward a higher good.

Jiang pivots from vows into a manifesto for the livestream: the class exists to share Dante with the world through a free, diverse, unrehearsed public classroom, and students will only truly understand Dante if they learn it in order to share it lovingly with a real person.
A short transitional interjection marks Jiang's pause before restating the key method for understanding Dante through loving transmission.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Likely Jiang filler or room echo

speaker_notes.note: The isolated 'Okay?' appears between two continuous Jiang monologue segments and is probably Jiang, but the diarization leaves it unknown.

claims.claim: Jiang says that to be fully human a person must get into the habit of making vows to himself or herself, because vows motivate movement toward a higher good.
claims.temporal_scope: Anthropological and ethical claim stated on 2026-06-17.

claims.claim: He defines making a vow as an expression of hope, love, and faith, and tells the class these three ideas will organize the next two days of discussion.
claims.temporal_scope: Definition and forward-looking class framing stated on 2026-06-17.

claims.claim: Jiang says the class is uniquely structured by three features: it is free, it contains an unusually diverse set of students, and it live streams everything without rehearsal.
He presents the mission of the class as proving to the world that anyone anywhere, regardless of culture or age, can read and love Dante.
Jiang argues that students will only truly understand Dante if they study him so they can later teach or share him with someone they really love, as an act of love.
claims.temporal_scope: Pedagogical and ethical method stated on 2026-06-17.

signature_moments.moment: Making vows is turned from a narrow religious act into a daily human technology for generating hope, love, and faith.
signature_moments.source_phrase: to be fully human, you must get into the habit of making vows to yourself
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It reframes a medieval theological category as a modern practice of self-formation and becomes the launch point for Jiang's whole virtue framework.

signature_moments.moment: The trick for learning Dante is to learn him in order to teach him as an act of love.
signature_moments.source_phrase: learn Dante... may teach it as an act of love
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is Jiang's compact formula for how understanding and love become inseparable in the classroom.

signature_moments.moment: The class is imagined as a co-created room whose real task is to let the whole world listen in and fall in love with Dante.
signature_moments.source_phrase: co-create together a classroom so that everyone in the world can listen in and love Dante
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It gives the livestream a missionary-public shape and explains why Jiang treats the classroom itself as part of the argument.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: For Jiang, not just a formal oath to God but a repeated self-binding practice that generates hope, love, faith, and direction toward a higher good.
Jiang's phrase for the right way to study and transmit Dante: reading, learning, debating, and teaching as a concrete gift to someone real.

chronology_notes.note: On 2026-06-17 the seminar moves directly from a practical question about vows into Jiang's broader manifesto for the class and for the public mission of teaching Dante.

uncertainty_notes.note: The transcript renders Dante as 'Donnie' here, but the context clearly shows Jiang is attributing the vow framework to Dante's teaching rather than to a different person.
